issues.title: DB switching behavior conflicts with “uncommitted UI edits” model
issues.evidence: Decision 17: “Switching DBs closes the current one (committing any pending edits) …” vs US-010: “Status bar shows ‘Unsaved’ while a cell edit is in progress but not yet committed.”
issues.recommendation: Define a single, testable rule for “pending edits” during DB switch/close: if there are in-progress UI edits not yet written to SQLite, block the switch with a 3-option prompt: (1) Save/Commit edit, (2) Discard edit, (3) Cancel. Do not auto-commit implicitly. Apply the same rule to tab close (beforeunload) warnings.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E checklist: (1) Start editing a cell but do not press Enter; attempt to switch to another DB; verify prompt appears. (2) Choose Cancel → no switch, edit remains. (3) Choose Discard → switch occurs, value not changed after returning. (4) Choose Save → switch occurs, value persists after returning + hard refresh.

issues.title: Persisted database registry / storage layout is required but not specified
issues.evidence: US-010: “User can delete a persisted database … removes DB file, associated metadata files … and registry entry from OPFS/IndexedDB” and “On app load, previously opened/imported databases appear in the sidebar.” Also naming rules: “Renaming updates the OPFS storage key and all metadata references (including ERD layout positions).”
issues.recommendation: Specify the persistence data model explicitly: (a) OPFS directory layout and naming conventions (DB file name incl. extension or not), (b) how the app enumerates existing DBs on startup, (c) the registry format (if used) with schema versioning, and (d) exact rename/delete semantics (atomicity expectations, how to handle partial failures, how to garbage-collect orphaned metadata like .erd.json).
issues.acceptanceTest: Automated tests: (1) Create DB A + metadata, refresh → A appears. (2) Rename A→B → DB file and metadata renamed, no orphan remains. (3) Delete B → DB file, metadata files, and registry entry removed; refresh → B absent. (4) Corrupt registry file (if used) → app recovers by re-indexing OPFS/IndexedDB without data loss.

issues.title: Size warnings are inconsistent between OPFS (100MB target) and IndexedDB fallback (50MB recommended)
issues.evidence: US-001: “Handle databases up to 100MB…” and “Files >100MB are accepted with a warning…” vs “Fallback contract (IndexedDB mode): Max recommended DB size: 50MB… Files >50MB show a warning.”
issues.recommendation: Make the warning thresholds storage-mode aware and consistent across the app: in IndexedDB fallback mode, warn at 50MB (and clarify that 100MB targets/guarantees do not apply). Ensure the same warning appears for import, on-open, and when DB grows past the threshold via edits/imports.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Run in IndexedDB mode, import a 60MB DB → warning shown immediately and in status bar. Run in OPFS mode, import 60MB → no warning; import 120MB → warning shown.

issues.title: CSV/JSON type auto-detection is underspecified (risk of surprising schemas)
issues.evidence: US-008 Acceptance Criteria: “Auto-detect column types (INTEGER, REAL, TEXT)” (no algorithm/precedence rules, sampling strategy, or override).
issues.recommendation: Define the inference algorithm (sample size, precedence, handling of leading zeros, scientific notation, empty fields/NULLs, mixed numeric/text). Add a per-column override in the preview step (dropdown: INTEGER/REAL/TEXT) so users can correct inference before import.
issues.acceptanceTest: Unit/E2E: Import CSV where a column includes values [
] → default should be TEXT (or explicitly documented rule). Verify user can override to INTEGER/REAL/TEXT and resulting schema matches selection.

issues.title: LIKE escaping is stated but missing a concrete SQL contract (escape character + ESCAPE clause)
issues.evidence: US-006 WHERE semantics: “User `%` and `_` input is escaped in LIKE patterns.” US-007 filters: “% and _ in user input are escaped.”
issues.recommendation: Specify the escape character (e.g., backslash) and require generated SQL to include an explicit `ESCAPE` clause (e.g., `LIKE ? ESCAPE '\'`). Define how to escape the escape character itself (e.g., `\`), and ensure the same logic is shared across query builder + grid filters.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Insert values containing literal `%` and `_` (e.g., “100%”, “a_b”). Filter for “%” and “_” and verify literal matches are returned (not treated as wildcards).

issues.title: FK creation validation needs clearer NULL semantics + a performance plan for large tables
issues.evidence: US-004: “FK creation with existing data violations… lists up to 10 sample violating rows with a total violation count.” (No definition of how NULL child keys are treated; no approach for counting/sampling efficiently.)
issues.recommendation: Define validation semantics explicitly: child FK columns that are NULL should be treated as non-violations (SQLite FK behavior). Specify a two-query approach: (1) sample query with `LIMIT 10`, (2) count query for total, both using the exact same predicate. Add progress/cancel for large datasets.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Child table has FK column NULL in some rows → FK creation should succeed if all non-NULL values match parent. Performance test: 1M-row child table with 1% violations → validation shows progress and completes without freezing; sample includes violating row identifiers.

issues.title: Dependency warnings vs “prefer native ALTER TABLE” needs a unified, authoritative dependency list
issues.evidence: US-003: “Prefer native ALTER TABLE… when available (SQLite >= 3.45).” and also “If dropping a column that is referenced by an index, FK, trigger, or view, show a dependency warning listing all affected objects before confirmation.”
issues.recommendation: Define dependency discovery as a layered approach for *all* schema mutations (native ALTER or rebuild): use PRAGMAs for indexes/FKs (authoritative) and `sqlite_master` scanning for views/triggers (best-effort), then rely on post-change compile-check as the final authority. Make it explicit that the warning list may be incomplete but the post-change verification is definitive and will rollback on breakage.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Create a view and trigger referencing a soon-to-be-dropped column; attempt drop via designer; verify preflight warns, and post-change compile-check rolls back with explicit broken object list if anything breaks.

issues.title: Read-only mode UX is defined, but statement-level behavior in SQL editor is not fully testable
issues.evidence: US-010 Multi-tab policy: “SQLite connection is opened with SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY… Any attempted write returns a consistent toast error: ‘Database is read-only.’ The data grid, query editor (SELECT only), and export all remain functional.”
issues.recommendation: Add a deterministic rule for SQL editor enforcement: pre-parse/prepare each statement and block any statement that would write (DML/DDL and write-PRAGMAs like `PRAGMA user_version=...`) before execution, emitting the standard toast. Still keep SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY as the hard backstop.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Open DB read-only (second tab). Run `SELECT 1` → succeeds. Run `CREATE TABLE x(a)` and `PRAGMA user_version=1` → blocked with toast before execution; DB unchanged.

issues.title: Query history lacks persistence/retention/clear policy (privacy + UX)
issues.evidence: US-005: “Query history (last 50 queries) accessible via dropdown” (no scope on persistence across reloads, per-DB vs global, or ability to clear).
issues.recommendation: Specify: (a) whether history persists across sessions, (b) whether it is per-database or global, (c) storage location (local-only, e.g., IndexedDB/localStorage), and (d) a “Clear history” control. Default to local-only persistence with explicit clear.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Execute 3 queries, refresh page → history persists (if specified). Use “Clear history” → dropdown empties and stays empty after refresh.

issues.title: CSV export can enable spreadsheet formula injection when opened in Excel/Sheets
issues.evidence: US-009 export rules define CSV output but do not address cells beginning with formula triggers (commonly `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`).
issues.recommendation: Add a safety option in export dialog: “Harden for Excel/Sheets (prefix risky leading chars)” default ON, with clear explanation. Apply to CSV exports only (tables/results), not to DB download. Preserve raw export option for power users.
issues.acceptanceTest: Unit test: exporting a value starting with `=1+1` results in a prefixed safe representation when hardening is enabled, and exact original when disabled.

suggestions.title: Define a single “SQL generation/quoting” utility contract used everywhere
suggestions.description: Identifier quoting and LIKE escaping appear in multiple features (designer, query builder, grid filters). Centralizing prevents subtle inconsistencies and injection footguns.
suggestions.recommendation: Create a documented utility layer: `quoteIdent()`, `escapeLikeLiteral()`, `buildWhereClause()` shared by query builder + grid filters + designer previews; add unit tests for tricky identifiers (quotes, dots, reserved words) and patterns.
suggestions.rationale: Reduces duplicate logic, makes SQL output deterministic, and improves testability and security posture.

suggestions.title: Add a “Recovery” flow for IndexedDB snapshot failures/corruption
suggestions.description: The PRD warns about degraded persistence and suggests export, but doesn’t define a concrete recovery UX beyond warnings.
suggestions.recommendation: Add: (1) auto-keep last N snapshots (e.g., 2) in IndexedDB with timestamps, (2) on load failure offer “Restore previous snapshot” vs “Open read-only (best effort)” vs “Delete local copy”.
suggestions.rationale: Turns scary storage edge cases into a controlled, user-trust-preserving workflow.

suggestions.title: Standardize all destructive actions around one confirmation + diff preview pattern
suggestions.description: Designer/ERD already use DDL diff preview + confirmation; grid delete confirms; SQL editor does not confirm (by design).
suggestions.recommendation: Document the rule: UI-driven destructive ops always show diff/confirm; SQL editor never confirms. Add a settings toggle: “Confirm destructive SQL (DROP/DELETE without WHERE)” default OFF.
suggestions.rationale: Clarifies boundaries and prevents accidental data loss without diluting the power-user story.

suggestions.title: Define a consistent error taxonomy and surface area (toast vs inline vs modal)
suggestions.description: Many features mention “clear error” but not a consistent mapping. Consistency is critical for a tool that will hit many edge cases.
suggestions.recommendation: Add a short section: categorize errors into (a) inline form errors, (b) non-blocking toasts, (c) blocking modals (quota exceeded, save failed after retries), and define required payload fields (code, message, details, remediation).
suggestions.rationale: Makes UX predictable and makes automated testing simpler (assert by error code).

suggestions.title: Add “Explain Query Plan” and “Time taken” for SQL editor and query builder
suggestions.description: You already have strong performance goals; exposing basic query timing helps users understand slow queries and validates performance work.
suggestions.recommendation: Show execution time + rows returned, and provide an “EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN” toggle that runs the explain and renders the output grid.
suggestions.rationale: Improves product usefulness with low implementation risk (leverages existing query execution + grid).

suggestions.title: Pin and expose the embedded SQLite version at runtime
suggestions.description: Several behaviors depend on SQLite >= 3.45 (DROP COLUMN, RIGHT JOIN).
suggestions.recommendation: Pin the SQLite version in build metadata and display `SELECT sqlite_version()` in an About/Diagnostics panel; add a startup assertion that fails fast (with a clear message) if the runtime version is below the required baseline.
suggestions.rationale: Prevents mysterious feature failures and strengthens support/debuggability.

suggestions.title: Make metadata migrations explicit for `<db-name>.erd.json` and future add-ons
suggestions.description: ERD metadata has a version field and forward-compat note, but no migration strategy if schema changes across app versions.
suggestions.recommendation: Add a small “Metadata migrations” section: rules for upgrading versions, how to handle downgrade, and a unit-tested migrator function keyed by `v`.
suggestions.rationale: Avoids subtle layout-loss regressions as features evolve.

strengths: Clear v1 scope boundaries and non-goals; avoids feature creep while still delivering a coherent Access-like core.
Acceptance criteria are unusually concrete and testable, with E2E IDs and specific behavioral assertions throughout.
Strong persistence design: OPFS direct VFS durability model is well-described, and IndexedDB fallback is thoughtfully constrained with explicit UX states.
Schema mutation strategy is robust: explicit preference for native ALTER when available, transactional rebuild fallback, and post-change compilation verification to prevent broken objects.
Security/trust section is pragmatic and implementation-oriented (CSP, escaping, worker isolation, no network after initial load).
Performance & scale targets include measurement methodology (CDP heap sampling, rAF frame timing, Lighthouse CI), which is rare and valuable.

overallAssessment.summary: This PRD is strong and unusually testable; addressing the two majors (DB switch semantics for in-progress edits, and the persistence registry/storage layout spec) should prevent the highest-risk rework and make implementation straightforward.
